name: priorityQueue
description: A data structure where each element has a priority. Extract-max (or extract-min) always returns the highest-priority element. Implemented with a binary heap: O(log n) insert/delete, O(1) peek.
aim: A Priority Queue always dequeues the element with the highest (or lowest) priority — not FIFO like a regular queue. Backed by a heap for O(log n) insert and extract.
howItWorks: Backed by a max-heap (or min-heap for min-priority queue)
Insert: add to end of heap, sift up to restore heap property
Extract-max: swap root with last element, remove last, sift down root
Peek: return root (highest priority) in O(1)

realWorld: CPU process scheduling: always run highest-priority process
Dijkstra's shortest path: always expand lowest-cost node
Huffman coding: always merge two lowest-frequency nodes
Hospital triage: always treat most critical patient
whenToUse: When you need to always process the most important item next
Graph algorithms needing minimum cost expansion
alternatives: Sorted array: O(n) insert but O(1) extract-max
Fibonacci heap: O(1) amortized insert, better for dense Dijkstra

beginnerAnalogy: Like a hospital emergency room — patients are seen in order of medical urgency, not arrival time. The most critical patient always goes to the front, no matter when they arrived.
beginnerWhat: A queue that always serves the highest-priority element first, not the oldest element.
beginnerWhy: Regular queues are FIFO — but many real problems need the most important item next, not the oldest.
beginnerWhen: Scheduling, pathfinding, greedy algorithms, any problem needing 'always pick the best option'.
